decisions.reason: The current wording is natural and the source can function as either an end-state title or action; shortening without exact control context risks changing that nuance.
The completed-race status is natural and semantically exact; the width excess is modest and does not justify a less natural rewrite by heuristic alone.
The current status accurately distinguishes the Challenge Race not yet appearing; a shorter 'chưa mở' form could alter the mechanic meaning.
The EXTREME availability label is clear, natural, and essentially within the width heuristic; no meaningful UI problem is established.
The VERY HARD availability label is clear and effectively at the heuristic width target; rewriting would be stylistic only.
'Carnival Đua' is visibly awkward mixed terminology, but changing the event name safely would require canonical event-name context and would otherwise drift into terminology curation.
'Nhóm hiện tại' is already compact, natural, and only slightly above the heuristic width target.
In a round/tab context, 'Vòng' is redundant; 'Chung kết' preserves the final-round meaning and fits the compact source much better.
The daily registration-count label is natural and effectively within the calculated width target; no rewrite is warranted.
The participation context is already established by the registration screen, so 'tham gia' is redundant in a fixed dialog title.
The source denotes the starters/race-card table; 'Bảng xuất phát' keeps the tab meaning while removing the wider 'Danh sách' construction.
'Không tham gia' is the clearest compact status; more aggressive shortening would risk changing or weakening the participation meaning.
The compact reward verb is natural on a button and removes the unnecessary generic noun 'phần'.
The colon form is a compact status relationship that preserves the next-WIN promotion condition without the wide helper phrase.
On an actionable matchmaking button, 'Bắt đầu' is redundant; the compact action remains unambiguous.
'Bảng xếp hạng' is a standard, compact Vietnamese UI term; shortening further would lose the table/standings nuance without enough benefit.
Matches the compact form for the identical reward-claim source and removes unnecessary width.
The current event label is natural and only slightly above the heuristic target; changing the event naming would be terminology work rather than justified UI shortening.
Uses the same compact final-round label as the identical source in Champions0003 and avoids needless width.
Within the Champions event screen, 'giải' supplies the hosting/event context more compactly than the awkward generic 'tổ chức'.
